claims.text: externalTrafficPolicy is a field of a Service's spec with the values Cluster and Local; Cluster is the default.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services > External traffic policy; API reference ServiceSpec.externalTrafficPolicy

claims.text: externalTrafficPolicy applies to traffic from outside the cluster that reaches a Service through its node ports or its load balancer address.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services > Traffic policies > External traffic policy ('traffic from external sources (NodePorts, ExternalIPs, and LoadBalancer IPs)')

claims.text: With externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster, the node receiving outside traffic replaces the source address with one of its own whichever Pod it picks (SNAT by default), and may forward it to a ready Pod on another node, so the Pod sees a node's address, not the client's.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tutorials > Services > Using Source IP (Source IP for Services with Type=NodePort / LoadBalancer); Virtual IPs and Service Proxies

claims.text: Under Cluster the node replaces the source address of outside traffic with one of its own. Because of that, a reply from a Pod on another node goes back through the receiving node, which returns it to the client.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tutorials > Services > Using Source IP (explanation of SNAT for NodePort: reply must go back through node)

claims.text: With externalTrafficPolicy: Local, kube-proxy sends outside traffic only to the Service's Pods on the receiving node and keeps the client's source address; a node with no local ready endpoint drops the packets.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies > External traffic policy ('only proxies to local endpoints', 'packets ... dropped'); Using Source IP

claims.text: For a Service with externalTrafficPolicy: Local, MetalLB's speakers in layer 2 mode announce the address only from nodes that run a ready endpoint of the Service; one of them announces at a time.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 / Usage > Traffic policies (Local: announce from nodes with ready endpoints); capture external-traffic-policy.txt last line; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-06 checked on donhang

claims.text: With Local in layer 2 mode only the Pods on the announcing node receive outside traffic, so load does not spread over Pods on other nodes; with Cluster kube-proxy picks a ready Pod per connection, so ten calls usually reach both Pods but can all land on one.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Usage > Traffic policies > Local traffic policy in layer 2 mode ('only the pods on that node receive traffic'); capture 'Pods that answered: 1'

claims.text: Choose Local when the application must see clients' addresses (logs, limits per client) and its Pods run on several nodes, so another node can announce if one Pod goes away; otherwise Cluster spreads load more evenly.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Usage > Traffic policies (trade-off Cluster vs Local); kubernetes.io Using Source IP
